judgments.reasoning_cat1: Territory 1 is defined residually — 'the remainder of the states of ... not listed in Territories 2' — so a risk in a listed state but an unlisted city must be classified by inference, and the state/city columns are scrambled in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This territory definition is superseded by Rating Schedule-A (c060) and then Amendment No. 2 (c066) and Schedule-B (c080), each with a different state list, so several versions coexist in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is dated 'Effective January 1, 1904' (plainly a mistake for 1994), describes the net profit as 'accruing to the REINSURED' when the accounting computes the reinsurer's result, and caps the article to 'the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits as respects each policy' without saying how premium and losses are split between layers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces only the first paragraph of Article VII, leaving the Accounting Schedule (c021), the net profit definition (c024) and the post-termination deferral (c025) — none of which is layer-limited — to be reconciled with the new $1,000,000 cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss arising out of the operation of a teaching hospital' drops the original's 'by the insured' qualifier and leaves 'teaching hospital' undefined, so a general hospital with a residency programme is arguably in or out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly deletes exclusion (a) of Article II (c005) for policies effective on or after July 1, 1995, so both versions live in the document and apply to different cessions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 350-bed threshold is arithmetically definite and the clause supplies its own enumerated definition of 'total beds'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the 250-bed version (c006) only for policies effective on or after July 1, 1995, so the applicable threshold turns on attachment date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named counties; nothing vague to identify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drops Cuyahoga County from the original exclusion (c008) at the same time as Rating Schedule-A (c061) prices Cleveland as Territory 3, which is coherent; the Michigan counties added here match the Schedule-A Territory 2 carve-out (c060).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limits are stated as '$25,000,000 each occurrence, $25,000,000 annual aggregate' with no statement of whether the aggregate is per policy, per insured or per treaty year, and the self-insured-retention proviso is a dense arithmetic exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the middle of three versions of Article III (c012 original, c076 substituted by Amendment No. 4), each with its own date trigger and different limits, so the applicable retention structure requires layering the amendments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line substitution of an attached schedule; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-A is later itself deleted and replaced by Schedule-B (c077), and Amendment No. 2 (c066) amends Schedule-A in the interim, so the chain of substitutions is layered but express.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In all other respects not inconsistent herewith' is the hinge phrase for every conflict between amendment and original, and its reach is precisely the sort of thing parties argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the relationship between Amendment No. 1's changes (c052-c056) and the untouched articles, notably the Accounting Schedule (c021) that the new contingent commission formula does not fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Arithmetic weightings, except the CRNA line 'each full-time equivalent x 5-10', which gives a range rather than a determinate factor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the original Rating Schedule (c050) and is itself replaced by Schedule-B (c079), which carries the same range forward.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Territory 1 is again residual and the Territory 2 table includes an entry — 'All areas except Wayne and Oakland County', Michigan — that is a state-wide carve-out rather than a city, sitting oddly in a list of cities/counties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Michigan appears in Territory 2 but not in the Territory 1 state list, and Amendment No. 2 (c066) later rewrites Territory 1 while Schedule-B (c080) drops Iowa, South Dakota, Washington and the Michigan entry again — a chain of inconsistent territory lists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two named entries with no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cleveland (Cuyahoga County) is priced here although the original exclusion (d) (c008) barred Cuyahoga risks; Amendment No. 1 (c055) removed that exclusion at the same time, so the instrument is coherent for post-July 1995 policies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three multipliers stated numerically; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The multipliers match the territory definitions in c060 and c061 and are carried into Schedule-B (c082).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is missing and the entry reads only 'Applied to premium developed in OBE rating. -125', so it is impossible to tell whether the figure is a factor, a credit or a debit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The equivalent entries in Schedule-B (c084, c092, c098) give differing figures ('-125', '25', '-is'), so the intended value is not resolved elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple table of year-by-year credits with a stated mature rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-B (c085) states different figures for the same years (45% versus 35% in year two; 18% versus 15% mature), so the two schedules diverge, albeit by express substitution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The credits and the risk categories are set out in separated columns so that which credit attaches to which category depends on alignment, and unlike the Schedule-B version it does not say whether the credits apply to minimum premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-B's counterpart (c087) expressly excludes minimum premiums, which highlights the silence here, though Schedule-A is superseded for later policies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward substitution of a residual state list; nothing ambiguous is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule-B's Territory 1 (c080) omits Iowa, South Dakota and Washington, which this amendment had just added, leaving the two lists inconsistent unless the substitution of Schedule-B is read as superseding Amendment No. 2 entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not inconsistent herewith' is the standard but elastic reconciliation formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision that determines whether Amendment No. 2's Territory 1 survives the later substitution of Schedule-B (c077, c080).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A name-change substitution with a stated effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The renamed entity appears consistently in Amendment No. 4 and the Stipulation of Termination (c099), so the change is carried through.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same elastic 'not inconsistent herewith' formula, here attached to a purely nominal change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the treaty turns on the identity change, so its reconciling function is trivial.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It adds Nursing Home and Outpatient Facility Professional Liability and a 'claims-conversion basis' without defining any of them, and again keys attachment to underlying limits 'not less than' the Schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it substitutes the whole first paragraph of Article I with one confined to policies effective on or after October 1, 1996, leaving pre-October 1996 cessions governed by the original (c001) — the scope of the substitution must be reconciled with the amendment's own date trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added entries are duplicative and overlapping — 'Nursing Homes and Outpatient Facilities Professional Liability' and, immediately beneath, 'Outpatient Facility Professional Liability' with identical limits — which is a drafting error on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule of Underlying Limits (c002) uses 'each medical incident' units, and Amendment No. 4's Article III (c076) fixes separate $10,000,000 limits for the same business, so the entries must be read with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'More than five locations unless the primary Commercial General Liability and Professional Liability limits apply per location' leaves undefined what counts as a 'location' and whether the exception must be satisfied for every location.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the added nursing home coverage in Article I (c070) and the sub-limit in Article III(b) (c076), which it qualifies rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Exceed five stories in height' is definite, but 'fire resistive' is a construction-classification term of art that is not defined here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the other Amendment No. 4 nursing home exclusions and the added coverage grant in c070 without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Surgicenters, emergicenters, hospices or laboratories' are undefined facility types, and there is no catch-all, raising an expressio unius question about other freestanding outpatient facilities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 simultaneously extends the treaty to Outpatient Facility Professional Liability (c070, c071), so the boundary between covered outpatient facilities and these excluded facility types is a genuine whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is framed against facilities ('outpatient facilities with employed physicians who provide patient care') but the carve-back is framed against roles ('medical directors and other administrative positions'), so the two halves do not fit together grammatically or logically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read broadly it would swallow much of the Outpatient Facility Professional Liability coverage newly granted by Article I as amended (c070) and priced in the Facility Rating section of Schedule-B (c093).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — 'As respects claims made policy forms, each claim shall be deemed an occurrence hereunder' — interacts with a $25,000,000 'each occurrence and annual aggregate' limit in a way that leaves the aggregation unit and the per-policy/per-year reach genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the third version of Article III (see c012 and c056) and must be squared with the Schedule of Underlying Limits' 'each medical incident' wording (c002) and the separate $10,000,000 nursing home sub-limit it itself introduces.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line substitution of the attached rating schedule; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes Schedule-A as amended by Amendment No. 2 (c066), and whether the Amendment No. 2 territory changes survive is not stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In all other respects not inconsistent herewith' again supplies an elastic reconciliation standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision that determines how Amendment No. 4's new coverages, exclusions and Article III interact with the surviving original articles (Article VII, Article XI) and with Amendment No. 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Arithmetic weightings, again with the indeterminate 'CRNA's — each full-time equivalent x 5-10' range.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reproduces the earlier schedules (c050, c059) and is consistent with the premium article (c018).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Territory 1 is defined residually by a state list, so risks in unlisted states have no stated territory at all — a genuine gap in the rating mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The state list here omits Iowa, South Dakota and Washington, which Amendment No. 2 (c066) had expressly added to Territory 1, and drops the Michigan and Seattle/Tacoma Territory 2 entries in c060 without explanation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two entries, one of which ('All cities', Alaska) is expressly comprehensive; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Territory 3 multiplier (c082) and the earlier Schedule-A version (c061).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three stated multipliers; purely arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: They correspond to the territory definitions in c080 and c081 with no mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incidental owned automobile exposure' is a vague threshold concept, though the two triggers that displace it (ambulances on emergency runs; more than 10 owned automobiles) are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001, c070) and the Schedule of Underlying Limits (c002) cover Automobile Liability, and this rating rule is consistent with that grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entry gives a bare number ('-125') without stating whether it is a multiplier, a credit or a percentage, and 'umbrella excluding BPL' appears to be a mistranscription of 'PL'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel entries in the Nursing Home and Facility sections of the same schedule (c092, c098) give different values, so the schedule does not resolve the figure internally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The table gives the same 35% credit for both the second and third years, which departs from the descending pattern and from the earlier schedule and looks like a transcription or drafting error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Rating Schedule-A (c064) sets 45% for the second year and an 18% mature rate, so the substituted table conflicts with its predecessor, though by express substitution under c077.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Promising that 'an extended reporting endorsement will be issued at no additional cost' if the insured continues on an occurrence basis leaves the reinsurance consequences of that free tail unaddressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I as amended (c070) recognises a 'claims-conversion basis' and Article I's discovery-period paragraph (c003) allows a separate limit of liability for such endorsements, so this free-tail promise interacts directly with the limit structure and the run-off rule in Article XI (c033).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two credits keyed to a bright-line bed count, with an express carve-out for minimum premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the minimum premium tables that follow in the same schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rate depends on 'OHIC's Manual GL and Professional Liability Premium (before application of experience and schedule rating)', a figure controlled by one party and not defined in the treaty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Facility Rating section (c093) uses the same construct with a different factor and refers to 'the REINSURED'S' manual premium, which is the same thing under Amendment No. 3 (c068).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allowing modification 'by schedule credit or debit at the REINSURED'S discretion but not to exceed 25% for a credit' caps credits but leaves debits uncapped and the discretion unstructured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Facility counterpart (c095) is drafted identically but names OHIC rather than the REINSURED; after Amendment No. 3 these are the same entity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of limits and the list of percentages are set out in separate blocks so that pairing them requires inference, and the total is described as 'the next $9,000,000' against ten enumerated millions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III as amended (c076(b)) caps nursing home business at $10,000,000 each occurrence, which matches the ten-million rating structure here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each million in limits is subject to a minimum premium of $1,000,000' states a minimum premium equal to the entire limit, which is commercially impossible and plainly a mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every other minimum premium table in the schedules is expressed in thousands (c097 aside), so the figure cannot be reconciled with the rest of the rating structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bare figures '25' and '258' are given without units and differ from the corresponding entries elsewhere in the same schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Hospital and Facility versions of the same line (c084, c098) give '-125' and '-is'/'25', so the schedule contradicts itself on the Indiana/Wisconsin factor and the contingent-endorsement charge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carves out 'Imaging (MRI) risks' from the general method and keys the rest to the REINSURED's own manual premium, both workable but dependent on undefined classifications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Nursing Home section (c088) and the outpatient facility coverage added by Amendment No. 4 (c070), though exclusion (j) (c074) removes laboratories and surgicenters from cover altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A receipts-based rate table with stated figures; 'receipts' is undefined but the mechanic is otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers back to 'the First Million rates and the excess factors from the preceding paragraph' for owned automobiles, a cross-reference that resolves against c093.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Discretionary schedule credit or debit capped only on the credit side, exercisable at OHIC's discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the Nursing Home credit provision (c089) and does not conflict with the minimum premium provisions it expressly excepts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean list of descending percentages applied to a defined 'modified First Million price'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the Facility rating base in c093 and c095 and with the ten-million structure used elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A minimum premium of '$1,500,000' for the first million of cover, and '$1,000,000' for each additional million, is on its face an impossible figure and reads as a misplaced decimal or dropped qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The hospital minimum premium tables in the same schedule run in thousands, so this entry cannot be reconciled with the rating structure as a whole; the Nursing Home version (c091) repeats the same error.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The values are given as bare, partly illegible figures ('-is', '25') with no units or explanation of application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The two parallel entries in the same schedule (c084, c092) give different numbers for what appears to be the same factor, an inconsistency the instrument does not resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination is expressed 'with respect to loss under policies issued on or after January 1, 1998' — 'issued' is a different trigger from the 'becoming effective' language used throughout Article I, and the sentence does not say what happens to losses under earlier policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI (c033) provides its own termination machinery — 90 days' notice, continuation of in-force policies for up to '12 months plus odd time', and continued cover for attaching discovery periods — none of which this stipulation addresses, so the run-off obligations after 1 January 1998 must be reconciled between the two.
